caption: The drawing shows three objects arranged vertically on a plain, light tan background. The top object is a rectangular metal lock box with rounded corners and a dark brown-black oxidized surface. The front face features a keyhole near the bottom and three small round holes, likely for screws, one in each corner except the lower right. An attached, curved handle or latch extends from the left side, made of the same dark metal. On the right side, a rectangular bolt protrudes outward. The middle object is a long, cylindrical key with a round bow (handle) on one end, made of a metallic brown color, and the bit (the toothed end that fits into the lock) is intricate with multiple cuts and grooves, indicating it is meant for a complex locking mechanism. The lower object is another view of the same lock box, but with the front plate removed, exposing the internal mechanism, including levers, a cylindrical bolt, pivot points, and an internal latch. This internal view also shows a socket for the key to be inserted. All objects occupy the center of the drawing vertically, with the key between the two views of the lock box, and all depicted with realistic tonal shading and metallic textures.
title: Zoar Lock w/ Key
